sanskrit: gatyā daśamyā te gatvā jaghnur vājirathadvipān hitvā nava gatīr duṣṭāḥ sa bāṇān vyāyato 'mucat
english: Moving by the tenth course, abandoning the nine evil courses, he advanced and slew horses, chariots, and elephants; that mighty one, drawing his bow at full stretch, loosed his shafts.

sanskrit: dināni daśa bhīṣmeṇa nighnatā tāvakaṃ balam śūnyāḥ kṛtā rathopasthā hatāś ca gajavājinaḥ
english: For ten days Bhīṣma, smiting your host, emptied the seats of the chariots and laid low elephants and horses.

sanskrit: darśayitvātmano rūpaṃ rudropendrasamaṃ yudhi pāṇḍavānām anīkāni pravigāhya vyaśātayat
english: Revealing in battle a form like Rudra's or Upendra's, he plunged into the ranks of the Pāṇḍavas and shattered them.

sanskrit: vinighnan pṛthivīpālāṃś cedipāñcālakekayān vyadahat pāṇḍavīṃ senāṃ narāśvagajasaṃkulām
english: Slaying the guardians of the earth—the Cedis, the Pāñcālas, the Kekayas—he consumed the Pāṇḍava army thronged with men, horses, and elephants.

sanskrit: majjantam aplave mandam ujjihīrṣuḥ suyodhanam tathā carantaṃ samare tapantam iva bhāskaram na śekuḥ sṛñjayā draṣṭuṃ tathaivānye mahīkṣitaḥ
english: Eager to rescue the foolish Suyodhana sinking in a sea without a raft, he ranged through the battle blazing like the sun, so that neither the Sṛñjayas nor the other kings of the earth could bear to look upon him.

sanskrit: vicarantaṃ tathā taṃ tu saṃgrāme jitakāśinam sarvodyogena sahasā pāṇḍavāḥ samupādravan
english: As he thus ranged through the fight with the radiance of victory, the Pāṇḍavas with all their might rushed suddenly upon him.

sanskrit: sa tu vidrāvya samare pāṇḍavān sṛñjayān api eka eva raṇe bhīṣma ekavīratvam āgataḥ
english: But routing in battle the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas alike, Bhīṣma, alone in the fray, attained to the rank of a single peerless hero.

sanskrit: taṃ śikhaṇḍī samāsādya tvayā gupto mahāratham jaghāna puruṣavyāghraṃ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: That mighty car-warrior, that tiger among men, Śikhaṇḍin—guarded by you—closed with and struck down with his straight-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: sa eṣa patitaḥ śete śaratalpe pitāmahaḥ tvāṃ prāpya puruṣavyāghra gṛdhraḥ prāpyeva vāyasam
english: There the grandsire lies fallen upon his bed of arrows, having met you, O tiger among men, as a vulture meets a crow.

sanskrit: droṇaḥ pañca dināny ugro vidhamya ripuvāhinīḥ kṛtvā vyūhaṃ mahāyuddhe pātayitvā mahārathān
english: For five days the dread Droṇa scattered the armies of his foes; arraying his battle-formation in the great war, he brought down mighty car-warriors.

sanskrit: jayadrathasya samare kṛtvā rakṣāṃ mahārathaḥ antakapratimaś cogrāṃ rātriṃ yuddhvādahat prajāḥ
english: That mighty car-warrior, guarding Jayadratha in the fight, fierce as Death itself, fought through the dreadful night and consumed living men.

sanskrit: adyeti dve dine vīro bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ samāsādya sa gataḥ paramāṃ gatim
english: For two days, counting today, the valiant hero, the son of Bharadvāja, fought; then, encountering Dhṛṣṭadyumna, he attained the supreme goal.

sanskrit: yadi caiva parān yuddhe sūtaputramukhān rathān nāvārayiṣyaḥ saṃgrāme na sma droṇo vyanaṅkṣyata
english: And had you not held off in the battle the enemy's car-warriors led by the sūta's son, Droṇa would never have perished in the fray.

sanskrit: bhavatā tu balaṃ sarvaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya vāritam tato droṇo hato yuddhe pārṣatena dhanaṃjaya
english: But by you the whole strength of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son was checked, and so Droṇa was slain in battle by Pṛṣata's grandson, O Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: ka ivānyo raṇe kuryāt tvad anyaḥ kṣatriyo yudhi yādṛśaṃ te kṛtaṃ pārtha jayadrathavadhaṃ prati
english: What other warrior, what other kṣatriya in battle, save you, could have done what you did, O Pārtha, in the slaying of Jayadratha?

sanskrit: nivārya senāṃ mahatīṃ hatvā śūrāṃś ca pārthivān nihataḥ saindhavo rājā tvayāstrabalatejasā
english: Having held back a mighty host and slain heroic kings, you laid low the king of the Sindhus by the might and splendor of your weapons.

sanskrit: āścaryaṃ sindhurājasya vadhaṃ jānanti pārthivāḥ anāścaryaṃ hi tat tvattas tvaṃ hi pārtha mahārathaḥ
english: The kings deem the slaying of the lord of the Sindhus a marvel; yet from you it is no marvel, for you, O Pārtha, are a mighty car-warrior.

sanskrit: tvāṃ hi prāpya raṇe kṣatram ekāhād iti bhārata tapyamānam asaṃyuktaṃ na bhaved iti me matiḥ
english: Once it has met you in battle, O Bhārata, the warrior class could not, even in a single day, remain unbroken and at ease—such is my conviction.

sanskrit: seyaṃ pārtha camūr ghorā dhārtarāṣṭrasya saṃyuge hatā sasarvavīrā hi bhīṣmadroṇau yadā hatau
english: This terrible army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, O Pārtha, with all its heroes, was as good as slain in the fray the moment Bhīṣma and Droṇa fell.

sanskrit: śīrṇapravarayodhādya hatavājinaradvipā hīnā sūryendunakṣatrair dyaur ivābhāti bhāratī
english: With its foremost warriors broken, its horses, men, and elephants slain, the Bhārata host today shines like the sky bereft of sun, moon, and stars.

sanskrit: vidhvastā hi raṇe pārtha seneyaṃ bhīmavikramāt āsurīva purā senā śakrasyeva parākramaiḥ
english: This army has been shattered in battle, O Pārtha, by Bhīma's prowess, as of old the host of the Asuras was shattered by the might of Śakra.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ hatāvaśiṣṭās tu pañca santi mahārathāḥ aśvatthāmā kṛtavarmā karṇo madrādhipaḥ kṛpaḥ
english: Of them, when the slain are counted, there remain but five mighty car-warriors: Aśvatthāman, Kṛtavarman, Karṇa, the lord of the Madras, and Kṛpa.

sanskrit: tāṃs tvam adya naravyāghra hatvā pañca mahārathān hatāmitraḥ prayacchorvīṃ rājñaḥ sadvīpapattanām
english: Slaying today these five mighty car-warriors, O tiger among men, and so destroying your foes, bestow upon the king the earth with its islands and cities.

sanskrit: sākāśajalapātālāṃ saparvatamahāvanām prāpnotv amitavīryaśrīr adya pārtho vasuṃdharām
english: May Pārtha of measureless valor and glory today win the earth, with its sky and waters and nether realms, with its mountains and its great forests.

sanskrit: etāṃ purā viṣṇur iva hatvā daiteyadānavān prayaccha medinīṃ rājñe śakrāyeva yathā hariḥ
english: As of old Viṣṇu, having slain the Daityas and Dānavas, gave the earth to Śakra, so do you, O Hari-like one, bestow this earth upon the king.

sanskrit: adya modantu pāñcālā nihateṣv ariṣu tvayā viṣṇunā nihateṣv eva dānaveyeṣu devatāḥ
english: Today let the Pāñcālas rejoice when their foes are slain by you, even as the gods rejoiced when the sons of Danu were slain by Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: yadi vā dvipadāṃ śreṣṭha droṇaṃ mānayato gurum aśvatthāmni kṛpā te 'sti kṛpe cācāryagauravāt
english: But if, O best of men, out of reverence for Droṇa your teacher, you feel pity for Aśvatthāman, or for Kṛpa from regard for a preceptor's dignity—

sanskrit: atyantopacitān vā tvaṃ mānayan bhrātṛbāndhavān kṛtavarmāṇam āsādya na neṣyasi yamakṣayam
english: or if, honoring those bound to you by long and close kinship, you will not, on meeting Kṛtavarman, send him to the abode of Yama—

sanskrit: bhrātaraṃ mātur āsādya śalyaṃ madrajanādhipam yadi tvam aravindākṣa dayāvān na jighāṃsasi
english: and if, meeting your mother's brother Śalya, the lord of the Madra people, you, O lotus-eyed one, in your compassion will not seek to slay him—

sanskrit: imaṃ pāpamatiṃ kṣudram atyantaṃ pāṇḍavān prati karṇam adya naraśreṣṭha jahy āśu niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: yet this wicked-minded, base Karṇa, ever utterly hostile to the Pāṇḍavas—him, O best of men, slay this day swiftly with your whetted shafts.

sanskrit: etat te sukṛtaṃ karma nātra kiṃ cin na yujyate vayam apy atra jānīmo nātra doṣo 'sti kaś cana
english: This will be a righteous deed of yours; nothing here is unfitting. We too know this well: in this there is no fault whatever.

sanskrit: dahane yat saputrāyā niśi mātus tavānagha dyūtārthe yac ca yuṣmāsu prāvartata suyodhanaḥ tatra sarvatra duṣṭātmā karṇo mūlam ihārjuna
english: In the burning of your mother and her sons by night, O sinless one, and in the gambling-match wherein Suyodhana moved against you all—in all of this, O Arjuna, the wicked-souled Karṇa was the root.

sanskrit: karṇād dhi manyate trāṇaṃ nityam eva suyodhanaḥ tato mām api saṃrabdho nigrahītuṃ pracakrame
english: For Suyodhana ever looks to Karṇa for his protection; and so, emboldened, he set out to lay hold even of me.

sanskrit: sthirā buddhir narendrasya dhārtarāṣṭrasya mānada karṇaḥ pārthān raṇe sarvān vijeṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: Firm, O bestower of honor, is the conviction of the king, Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, that Karṇa will conquer all the Pārthas in battle, beyond all doubt.

sanskrit: karṇam āśritya kaunteya dhārtarāṣṭreṇa vigrahaḥ rocito bhavatā sārdhaṃ jānatāpi balaṃ tava
english: Relying upon Karṇa, O son of Kuntī, Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son chose strife with you, though he knew full well your strength.

sanskrit: karṇo hi bhāṣate nityam ahaṃ pārthān samāgatān vāsudevaṃ sarājānaṃ vijeṣyāmi mahāraṇe
english: For Karṇa ever boasts: 'I shall conquer the assembled Pārthas, and Vāsudeva, and the king with them, in the great battle.'

sanskrit: protsāhayan durātmānaṃ dhārtarāṣṭraṃ sudurmatiḥ samitau garjate karṇas tam adya jahi bhārata
english: Inciting the evil-souled son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, that most malign Karṇa roars in the assembly—slay him this day, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yac ca yuṣmāsu pāpaṃ vai dhārtarāṣṭraḥ prayuktavān tatra sarvatra duṣṭātmā karṇaḥ pāpamatir mukham
english: And in every wrong that Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son has wrought against you, the wicked-souled, evil-minded Karṇa has been the foremost agent.

sanskrit: yac ca tad dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ krūraiḥ ṣaḍbhir mahārathaiḥ apaśyaṃ nihataṃ vīraṃ saubhadram ṛṣabhekṣaṇam
english: And when I beheld the hero, the son of Subhadrā, with the eyes of a bull, slain by six cruel mighty car-warriors of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's side—

sanskrit: droṇadrauṇikṛpān vīrān kampayanto mahārathān nirmanuṣyāṃś ca mātaṅgān virathāṃś ca mahārathān
english: he who made the heroes Droṇa, Droṇa's son, and Kṛpa, mighty car-warriors, tremble; who emptied elephants of their riders and stripped great car-warriors of their cars—

sanskrit: vyaśvārohāṃś ca turagān pattīn vyāyudhajīvitān kurvantam ṛṣabhaskandhaṃ kuruvṛṣṇiyaśaskaram
english: who left horses without their riders and footmen bereft of weapons and life—that bull-shouldered youth, the glory of the Kurus and Vṛṣṇis—

sanskrit: vidhamantam anīkāni vyathayantaṃ mahārathān manuṣyavājimātaṅgān prahiṇvantaṃ yamakṣayam
english: who scattered the ranks and confounded the mighty car-warriors, dispatching men, horses, and elephants to the abode of Yama—

sanskrit: śaraiḥ saubhadram āyastaṃ dahantam iva vāhinīm tan me dahati gātrāṇi sakhe satyena te śape
english: the son of Subhadrā, straining at the work, consuming the host as it were with his arrows—the memory of this burns my very limbs, my friend; I swear it to you in truth.

sanskrit: yat tatrāpi ca duṣṭātmā karṇo 'bhyadruhyata prabho aśaknuvaṃś cābhimanyoḥ karṇaḥ sthātuṃ raṇe 'grataḥ
english: And there too the wicked-souled Karṇa wrought him harm, O lord—Karṇa, who could not stand before Abhimanyu in the forefront of battle.

sanskrit: saubhadraśaranirbhinno visaṃjñaḥ śoṇitokṣitaḥ niḥśvasan krodhasaṃdīpto vimukhaḥ sāyakārditaḥ
english: Pierced by the arrows of Subhadrā's son, swooning, drenched in blood, breathing hard, inflamed with rage, turned away and tormented by the shafts—

sanskrit: apayānakṛtotsāho nirāśaś cāpi jīvite tasthau suvihvalaḥ saṃkhye prahārajanitaśramaḥ
english: bent on flight, and despairing even of his life, he stood there utterly distraught in the fray, worn out by the blows he had taken.

sanskrit: atha droṇasya samare tat kālasadṛśaṃ tadā śrutvā karṇo vacaḥ krūraṃ tataś ciccheda kārmukam
english: Then in the battle Karṇa, hearing the cruel counsel of Droṇa, fitting to that hour of doom, thereupon cut through the youth's bow.

sanskrit: tataś chinnāyudhaṃ tena raṇe pañca mahārathāḥ sa caiva nikṛtiprajñaḥ prāvadhīc charavṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: Then, his weapon severed by that one of crafty cunning, the five mighty car-warriors—and he himself—struck him down in the fray with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: yac ca karṇo 'bravīt kṛṣṇāṃ sabhāyāṃ paruṣaṃ vacaḥ pramukhe pāṇḍaveyānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca nṛśaṃsavat
english: And the harsh words that Karṇa spoke to Kṛṣṇā in the assembly, before the very faces of the Pāṇḍavas and the Kurus, like a man without mercy—

sanskrit: vinaṣṭāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ kṛṣṇe śāśvataṃ narakaṃ gatāḥ patim anyaṃ pṛthuśroṇi vṛṇīṣva mitabhāṣiṇi
english: 'The Pāṇḍavas are ruined, O Kṛṣṇā; they have gone to everlasting hell. Choose another lord, O broad-hipped, soft-spoken one.'

sanskrit: lekhābhru dhṛtarāṣṭrasya dāsī bhūtvā niveśanam praviśārālapakṣmākṣi na santi patayas tava
english: 'O delicately-browed, O you with curving lashes and lovely eyes, become a slave and enter the household of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; your husbands are no more.'

sanskrit: ity uktavān adharmajñas tadā paramadurmatiḥ pāpaḥ pāpaṃ vacaḥ karṇaḥ śṛṇvatas tava bhārata
english: Thus that knower of no righteousness, that most malign and sinful Karṇa, spoke his sinful words within your very hearing, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tasya pāpasya tad vākyaṃ suvarṇavikṛtāḥ śarāḥ śamayantu śilādhautās tvayāstā jīvitacchidaḥ
english: Let your gold-wrought arrows, whetted upon stone and life-severing, shot by you, silence forever the speech of that sinner.

sanskrit: yāni cānyāni duṣṭātmā pāpāni kṛtavāṃs tvayi tāny adya jīvitaṃ cāsya śamayantu śarās tava
english: And whatever other evils the wicked-souled one has wrought against you—let your shafts this day quiet them all, together with his life.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvaprahitān ghorān adya gātraiḥ spṛśañ śarān karṇaḥ smaratu duṣṭātmā vacanaṃ droṇabhīṣmayoḥ
english: As his limbs feel today the dreadful shafts sped from the Gāṇḍīva, let the wicked-souled Karṇa remember the words of Droṇa and Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: suvarṇapuṅkhā nārācāḥ śatrughnā vaidyutaprabhāḥ tvayāstās tasya marmāṇi bhittvā pāsyanti śoṇitam
english: Your gold-feathered iron shafts, slayers of foes, bright as lightning, loosed by you, shall pierce his vitals and drink his blood.

sanskrit: ugrās tvadbhujanirmuktā marma bhittvā śitāḥ śarāḥ adya karṇaṃ mahāvegāḥ preṣayantu yamakṣayam
english: Let the fierce, keen shafts loosed from your arm, swift and rending the vitals, send Karṇa this day to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: adya hāhākṛtā dīnā viṣaṇṇās tvaccharārditāḥ prapatantaṃ rathāt karṇaṃ paśyantu vasudhādhipāḥ
english: Today let the lords of the earth, crying out in dismay, wretched and stricken by your shafts, behold Karṇa toppling from his chariot.

sanskrit: adya svaśoṇite magnaṃ śayānaṃ patitaṃ bhuvi apaviddhāyudhaṃ karṇaṃ paśyantu suhṛdo nijāḥ
english: Today let his own kinsmen and friends behold Karṇa sunk in his own blood, lying fallen upon the earth, his weapon flung aside.

sanskrit: hastikakṣyo mahān asya bhallenonmathitas tvayā prakampamānaḥ patatu bhūmāv ādhirather dhvajaḥ
english: Struck down by your broad-headed arrow, let the great elephant-girth standard of Adhiratha's son tremble and fall to the ground.

sanskrit: tvayā śaraśataiś chinnaṃ rathaṃ hemavibhūṣitam hatayodhaṃ samutsṛjya bhītaḥ śalyaḥ palāyatām
english: Let Śalya in his terror flee, abandoning the gold-adorned chariot, its warrior slain, its frame riddled by your hundreds of shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ suyodhano dṛṣṭvā hatam ādhirathiṃ tvayā nirāśo jīvite tv adya rājye caiva dhanaṃjaya
english: Then, beholding Adhiratha's son slain by you, let Suyodhana this day despair of his life and of his kingdom alike, O Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: ete dravanti pāñcālā vadhyamānāḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ karṇena bharataśreṣṭha pāṇḍavān ujjihīrṣavaḥ
english: See, O best of the Bhāratas, the Pāñcālas, eager to rescue the Pāṇḍavas, take flight as they are cut down by Karṇa's keen arrows.

sanskrit: pāñcālān draupadeyāṃś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaśikhaṇḍinau dhṛṣṭadyumnatanūjāṃś ca śatānīkaṃ ca nākulim
english: The Pāñcālas, the sons of Draupadī, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, the sons of Dhṛṣṭadyumna, and Śatānīka the son of Nakula—

sanskrit: nakulaṃ sahadevaṃ ca durmukhaṃ janamejayam suvarmāṇaṃ sātyakiṃ ca viddhi karṇavaśaṃ gatān
english: Nakula and Sahadeva, Durmukha and Janamejaya, Suvarman and Sātyaki—know them all to have fallen under Karṇa's power.

sanskrit: abhyāhatānāṃ karṇena pāñcālānāṃ mahāraṇe śrūyate ninado ghoras tvadbandhūnāṃ paraṃtapa
english: The dreadful outcry of the Pāñcālas, your kinsmen, smitten by Karṇa in the great battle, is heard, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: na tv eva bhītāḥ pāñcālāḥ kathaṃ cit syuḥ parāṅmukhāḥ na hi mṛtyuṃ maheṣvāsā gaṇayanti mahārathāḥ
english: Yet never would the Pāñcālas, for all their fear, turn their backs; for those great archers, those mighty car-warriors, reckon death as nothing.

sanskrit: ya ekaḥ pāṇḍavīṃ senāṃ śaraughaiḥ samaveṣṭayat taṃ samāsādya pāñcālā bhīṣmaṃ nāsan parāṅmukhāḥ
english: He who alone encompassed the Pāṇḍava army with floods of arrows—even Bhīṣma—the Pāñcālas, when they met him, did not turn their backs upon.

sanskrit: tathā jvalantam astrāgniṃ guruṃ sarvadhanuṣmatām nirdahantaṃ samārohan durdharṣaṃ droṇam ojasā
english: So too they climbed in their might against the unassailable Droṇa, blazing like the fire of weapons, the preceptor of all bowmen, consuming all before him.

sanskrit: te nityam uditā jetuṃ yuddhe śatrūn ariṃdamāḥ na jātv ādhirather bhītāḥ pāñcālāḥ syuḥ parāṅmukhāḥ
english: Ever ready to conquer their foes in battle, those tamers of enemies, the Pāñcālas, would never out of fear of Adhiratha's son turn their backs.

sanskrit: teṣām āpatatāṃ śūraḥ pāñcālānāṃ tarasvinām ādatte 'sūñ śaraiḥ karṇaḥ pataṃgānām ivānalaḥ
english: As they rush upon him, the valiant Karṇa takes the lives of those swift Pāñcālas with his arrows, as fire devours moths.

sanskrit: tāṃs tathābhimukhān vīrān mitrārthe tyaktajīvitān kṣayaṃ nayati rādheyaḥ pāñcālāñ śataśo raṇe
english: Those heroes who thus front him, who lay down their lives for their friends' sake—the son of Rādhā brings them to destruction, the Pāñcālas by the hundred in battle.

sanskrit: astraṃ hi rāmāt karṇena bhārgavād ṛṣisattamāt yad upāttaṃ purā ghoraṃ tasya rūpam udīryate
english: The terrible weapon that Karṇa long ago received from Rāma of Bhṛgu's line, the most excellent of sages—its dreadful form now displays itself.

sanskrit: tāpanaṃ sarvasainyānāṃ ghorarūpaṃ sudāruṇam samāvṛtya mahāsenāṃ jvalati svena tejasā
english: Scorching all the armies, terrible of form and most dire, it enwraps the great host and blazes with its own splendor.

sanskrit: ete caranti saṃgrāme karṇacāpacyutāḥ śarāḥ bhramarāṇām iva vrātās tāpayantaḥ sma tāvakān
english: See how these arrows loosed from Karṇa's bow range through the battle like swarms of bees, scorching your warriors.

sanskrit: ete caranti pāñcālā dikṣu sarvāsu bhārata karṇāstraṃ samare prāpya durnivāram anātmabhiḥ
english: See how the Pāñcālas scatter in all directions, O Bhārata, meeting in battle Karṇa's weapon, irresistible by those who lack his command of self.

sanskrit: eṣa bhīmo dṛḍhakrodho vṛtaḥ pārtha samantataḥ sṛñjayair yodhayan karṇaṃ pīḍyate sma śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: There is Bhīma of unyielding wrath, O Pārtha, hemmed in on every side; fighting Karṇa with the Sṛñjayas about him, he is hard pressed by the keen shafts.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavān sṛñjayāṃś caiva pāñcālāṃś caiva bhārata hanyād upekṣitaḥ karṇo rogo deham ivātataḥ
english: If left unchecked, O Bhārata, Karṇa would destroy the Pāṇḍavas, the Sṛñjayas, and the Pāñcālas alike, as a spreading disease destroys the body.

sanskrit: nānyaṃ tvatto 'bhipaśyāmi yodhaṃ yaudhiṣṭhire bale yaḥ samāsādya rādheyaṃ svastimān āvrajed gṛham
english: I see no warrior in Yudhiṣṭhira's host save you who, having encountered the son of Rādhā, could return home unscathed.

sanskrit: tam adya niśitair bāṇair nihatya bharatarṣabha yathāpratijñaṃ pārtha tvaṃ kṛtvā kīrtim avāpnuhi
english: Slay him this day with your whetted arrows, O bull of the Bhāratas, and fulfilling your vow, O Pārtha, win renown.
